proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(P_s\) for the standard-form conic program supplied by \texttt{def:standard-conic-encoding}, with value in \([0,+\infty]\).  We first dispose of infeasibility.  For every \(j\in\mathcal J\) and \(0\leq h\leq K\), the definition of the donor sets gives
\[
 D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh},                                                   \tag{1}
\]
because \(T_i>T_j+K\) implies \(T_i>T_j+h\).  If \(P_{\mathrm{nested}}\) is feasible, its coordinate at horizon \(K\) belongs to \(\Delta(D_{jK})\) for every \(j\), so every deepest donor simplex is nonempty.  Reusing an arbitrary element of \(\Delta(D_{jK})\) at every horizon makes \(P_{\mathrm{deep}}\) feasible.  Conversely, (1) embeds each deep-feasible weight array in \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{nested}}\).  Once weights are feasible, all norm epigraphs and scalar slacks in \texttt{def:bonferroni-socp} can be chosen finite.  Hence
\[
 P_{\mathrm{nested}}\text{ is feasible}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 P_{\mathrm{deep}}\text{ is feasible}.                                  \tag{2}
\]
If (2) fails, both values are \(+\infty\), so the strict inequality is false.  A valid \(\mathsf{GapCert}\) is then impossible because its \(y_N\) is nested-primal feasible and its \(y^\circ\) is deep-primal feasible.  Thus the desired equivalence holds in the infeasible case.

Assume henceforth that the equivalent feasibility conditions in (2) hold.  Eliminating the epigraph variables for a fixed weight array yields
\[
 G_s(w)=\max_{(j,h)\in\mathcal E}
 \left\{
 L\left\|x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i\right\|_2+
 \delta+z_B\left\|R_Qa_{jh}(w)\right\|_2
 \right\}.                                                               \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, the smallest admissible \(u_{jh}\) and \(v_{jh}\) are the two norms in (3), and the smallest admissible \(g\) is their finite maximum.  Each nonempty donor simplex is closed and bounded in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, and hence compact; therefore the finite product \(\mathcal F_s\) is compact.  The affine maps in (3), Euclidean norms, and a finite maximum are continuous.  Consequently,
\[
 \Gamma_s=\min_{w\in\mathcal F_s}G_s(w)<+\infty,                          \tag{4}
\]
and the minimum is attained.  Restoring the norm values and nonnegative slacks gives an attained optimizer of \(P_s\).  This argument uses neither division nor a rank condition and allows zero donor weights and nonunique minimizers.

We next prove the forward implication.  Suppose
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}.                        \tag{5}
\]
Choose a nested primal optimizer \(y_N^*\), which exists by (4).  The cone \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm{deep}}\) is a finite product of nonnegative orthants, Lorentz cones, and zero cones, so it is a finite-dimensional closed convex cone.  Its affine feasible space
\[
 H_D=\{y:B_{\mathrm{deep}}y=d_{\mathrm{deep}}\}
\]
meets that cone by (2).  Applying \texttt{lem:facial-reduction-relative-strong-duality} gives a finite strict facial-reduction chain
\[
 \mathcal K_{\mathrm{deep}}=F_0\supsetneq F_1\supsetneq\cdots
 \supsetneq F_r=F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}                                  \tag{6}
\]
and a point
\[
 y^\circ\in H_D\cap\operatorname{ri}F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}.             \tag{7}
\]
Every strict inclusion in (6) lowers dimension, so the possible chain lengths form a finite set.

The exposing vectors in (6) may be put in the affine-multiplier form required by \texttt{def:facial-dual}.  At step \(k\), the exposing vector \(z_k\) annihilates \(H_D\), hence annihilates its direction space \(\ker B_{\mathrm{deep}}\).  Finite-dimensional linear algebra gives
\[
 z_k\in(\ker B_{\mathrm{deep}})^\perp
      =\operatorname{range}(B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}),
 \qquad
 z_k=B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\eta_k                                  \tag{8}
\]
for some multiplier \(\eta_k\).  If \(y_0\in H_D\), then
\[
 0=z_k^{\top}y_0
  =\eta_k^{\top}B_{\mathrm{deep}}y_0
  =\eta_k^{\top}d_{\mathrm{deep}}.                                     \tag{9}
\]
Thus (6)--(9) satisfy all exposure identities in \texttt{def:facial-dual}.  By (4), the deep primal value is finite.  The same cited facial-reduction lemma therefore supplies an attained facial-dual optimizer \(\lambda_D^*\) such that
\[
 c_{\mathrm{deep}}-B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D^*
       \in F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}^*,
 \qquad
 d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D^*=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}.          \tag{10}
\]
Together, (5), nested optimality, and (10) imply
\[
 c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N^*
 <d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D^*.                                 \tag{11}
\]

We now turn (6)--(11) into exact algebraic data without imposing ordinary Slater feasibility.  All relevant relations are semialgebraic over the rational input.  Orthant and zero-cone membership use linear inequalities and equalities.  Lorentz-cone membership is
\[
 (t,z)\in\mathcal L_q
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 t\geq0\ \text{ and }\ t^2-\sum_{\nu=1}^{q-1}z_\nu^2\geq0.            \tag{12}
\]
For clarity, the faces also have finite semialgebraic descriptions.  A face of a nonnegative orthant is specified by the coordinates fixed at zero.  A nonzero proper face of a Lorentz cone is a boundary ray: if it contained two noncollinear nonzero boundary points, their midpoint would satisfy the strict inequality in (12), and a cone face containing an interior point would be the entire cone.  Such a ray can be parameterized by a generator \((1,u)\) satisfying \(\|u\|_2=1\); the other two possibilities are the zero face and the full cone.  Finally, every face of a finite product cone is a product of faces.  Indeed, if \(F\) is a face of \(K_1\times K_2\) and \((x_1,x_2)\in F\), then
\[
 (x_1,x_2)=(x_1,0)+(0,x_2),                                             \tag{13}
\]
and the face property puts both summands in \(F\); closure under addition gives the reverse product inclusion.  Iterating proves the assertion.  Thus face membership, dual-face membership, relative-interior membership, strict inclusion, and the exposure equality \(F_k=F_{k-1}\cap z_k^\perp\) can each be expressed by a finite first-order formula whose atoms are rational polynomial sign conditions.  Clearing the finitely many rational denominators produces integer-coefficient atoms.

For every possible chain length \(r\), let \(\Psi_r\) assert the existence of face parameters, \(z_k,\eta_k,y^\circ,y_N,\lambda_D\) satisfying \texttt{def:facial-dual}, nested primal feasibility, facial-dual feasibility, and
\[
 c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N
 <d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D.                                   \tag{14}
\]
There are only finitely many \(r\) to consider.  Equations (6)--(11) show that (5) implies the truth of at least one \(\Psi_r\).  Conversely, suppose some \(\Psi_r\) holds.  Nested primal feasibility, facial-dual feasibility, and weak conic duality give
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}
 \leq c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N
 <d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D
 \leq\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}.                                           \tag{15}
\]
The last inequality follows directly: if \(y_D\) is any deep-feasible point and \(s_D=c_{\mathrm{deep}}-B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D\in F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}^*\), preservation of the feasible set under facial reduction gives \(y_D\in F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}\), and therefore
\[
 c_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}y_D-d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D
 =s_D^{\top}y_D\geq0.                                                   \tag{16}
\]
Taking the minimum over deep-feasible \(y_D\) proves the last inequality in (15).  Hence
\[
 \bigvee_r\Psi_r
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}.                      \tag{17}
\]

The narrowed \texttt{lem:effective-real-algebraic-elimination} now applies exactly at its attested scope.  Theorem 14.16 of the cited source eliminates the quantifiers in each \(\Psi_r\), terminates, and returns an equivalent quantifier-free formula.  Apply the sign-condition sampling algorithm of its Theorem 13.11 to the finite family of integer polynomials occurring in that formula.  It computes real-univariate sample representations meeting every nonempty semialgebraically connected component of every realizable sign condition and computes the signs of those input polynomials at the samples.  Testing the Boolean formula with those signs identifies a satisfying realizable sign condition whenever \(\Psi_r\) is true.  The degree and coefficient-size conclusions asserted by the narrowed cited lemma apply to this sampling call, but no runtime conclusion is drawn from them.

It remains to obtain witnesses in the precise representation \(\mathbb A_{\mathrm{rep}}\).  Let \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) denote the real algebraic numbers.  Both \(\mathbb R\) and \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) are real closed fields containing \(\mathbb Q\).  Quantifier elimination therefore makes every rational-coefficient sentence equivalent in either field to the same quantifier-free sentence with no variables.  Hence truth of an existential \(\Psi_r\) over \(\mathbb R\) implies truth over \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\), so an algebraic witness tuple exists.  Enumerate all finite tuples of square-free integer polynomials, rational isolating intervals, and root indices, and use effective real-closed-field checking to verify that each tuple represents real roots and satisfies \(\Psi_r\).  Every real algebraic number has such a representation, so the existing algebraic witness eventually appears and the enumeration terminates.  This gives exact \(\mathbb A_{\mathrm{rep}}\) entries for the chain, multipliers, and primal and dual points.  Rechecking the polynomial formulas certifies all equalities, cone signs, relative-interior conditions, and (14).  Together with (17), this supplies an exact terminating decision and algebraic-witness procedure for the strict gap.

Let
\[
 p_N=c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N,
 \qquad
 q_D=d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D.
\]
They are algebraic and (14) says \(p_N<q_D\).  To construct the two rational objective enclosures, enumerate rational quadruples \((\ell_N,u_N,\ell_D,u_D)\) and use effective real-closed-field checking to retain the first one satisfying
\[
 \ell_N\leq p_N\leq u_N<\ell_D\leq q_D\leq u_D.                         \tag{18}
\]
This search terminates.  Indeed, put \(\varepsilon=(q_D-p_N)/3>0\).  The Archimedean property gives an integer \(n\) with \(1/n<\varepsilon\); choosing successive integer grid points of mesh \(1/n\) around \(p_N\) and \(q_D\) gives rational outer intervals whose inner endpoints are strictly ordered.  Thus a quadruple satisfying (18) exists and eventually appears in the enumeration.  Setting \(I_N=[\ell_N,u_N]\) and \(I_D=[\ell_D,u_D]\) gives
\[
 c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N\in I_N,
 \qquad
 d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D\in I_D,
 \qquad
 \sup I_N<\inf I_D.                                                      \tag{19}
\]
The exact algebraic chain and points together with these intervals constitute a valid finite \(\mathsf{GapCert}\).  This proves existence of a certificate from the strict gap.  The converse is \texttt{prop:strict-gap-sufficient}; equivalently, it also follows from (15) and (19).

The verifier terminates for the same rate-free reason: it expresses every proposed face, affine, cone, relative-interior, root-isolation, root-index, and objective-enclosure check as a finite first-order sentence over a real closed field and applies the terminating quantifier-elimination algorithm.  Only the final rational interval arithmetic in (19) is outward-rounded.  No bound on bit operations, on the cost of interval separation, or on arbitrary algebraic sign determination is asserted.

The proof covers all boundary and degeneracy cases promised in the statement.  Zero donor weights are orthant-boundary points; redundant predictor columns merely repeat polynomial constraints; and (12) plus the face classification includes full, ray, and zero Lorentz faces, including collapsed blocks.  Relative-interior feasibility is used only after replacing the original cone by its minimal face.  No uniqueness, positive-weight, rank, ordinary Slater, or strict-complementarity assumption was introduced, and no limiting argument was used.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For a first-order formula over a real closed field whose atoms are polynomial sign conditions, effective quantifier elimination terminates and produces an equivalent quantifier-free formula.  Separately, for a finite family of \(s\) polynomials of degree at most \(D\) in \(k\) variables, sign-condition sampling computes real-univariate sample points meeting every semialgebraically connected component of every realizable sign condition and computes the signs of the input polynomials at those points.  The sampled univariate representations have degree \(O(D)^k\); when the input coefficients are integers of bitsize at most \(\tau\), their coefficient bitsizes are bounded by \(\tau D^{O(k)}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The attested text of Basu--Pollack--Roy Theorems 13.11 and 14.16 supports effective quantifier elimination, sign-condition sampling, input-polynomial signs, and the displayed representation degree and coefficient-bitsize bounds.  It does not state the former fixed-block bit-complexity bound or a same-envelope guarantee for arbitrary exact algebraic arithmetic and sign determination, so those clauses must be removed.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every finite rational input \(\mathsf{Data}\),
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{a valid finite }\mathsf{GapCert}\text{ exists}.
\]
There is an exact terminating construction and verifier: a finite disjunction of semialgebraic facial-reduction systems is decided by effective real-closed-field quantifier elimination, algebraic witnesses are represented in \(\mathbb A_{\mathrm{rep}}\), and rational objective enclosures are enumerated until they separate.  Outward-rounded rational arithmetic is used only for the two objective enclosures.  The equivalence and terminating algorithm require neither unique optimizers, positive donor weights, independent predictor columns, ordinary Slater feasibility, nor strict complementarity, and they cover tight and collapsed Lorentz-cone blocks.  No quantitative bit-complexity bound is asserted.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The exact finite if-and-only-if certificate and termination follow from facial reduction, effective real-closed-field decision, algebraic witness enumeration, and rational density.  The previous displayed bit-operation bound, its dependence on \(d\), \(B\), and the strict gap, and the positive-part necessity claim were not supported by the attested quantitative source text and are deleted.

prose_updates.tldr: Staggered adoption creates shrinking not-yet-treated donor sets. Conditional on the declared nonempty rational fixed design, this note maps every treated-unit--horizon error into one deduplicated Gaussian contrast vector and defines the jointly attainable bias set generated by the shared calendar-time coefficients and cellwise remainder bounds. The exact honest deterministic linear-band frontier is the attained minimum, over the relevant product of donor simplexes, of the worst shifted Gaussian-cube radius over that joint bias set. A fixed-Bonferroni bias-plus-standard-error SOCP remains finite-sample honest and within the stated dimension-uniform spectral factor of this exact frontier. A legal common-donor family with rational covariance factor proves that the square-root covariance-condition-number dependence is order-sharp for fixed Bonferroni calibration. Zero-bias Loewner and diagonal row-disjoint results give computable strict nested-width gains. Separately, an exact finite primal--facial-dual certificate characterizes strict improvement of the SOCP surrogate on degenerate faces and has a terminating real-algebraic construction and verifier; no quantitative runtime bound is claimed. Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein provide donor geometry only; \texttt{scpi} and \texttt{augsynth::multisynth} are implementation consumers, not estimators covered by these theorems.
prose_updates.related_work: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2022, Section 2) supply the shrinking not-yet-treated donor-set geometry and note that their estimator may use horizon-varying donors even though their exposition and application focus on a common deepest pool. They do not supply this note's bounded-mean known-covariance class, and no theorem here evaluates their partially pooled estimator. Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik (2025, Sections 4.4 and 6 and Supplemental Appendix S.6) provide staggered prediction-error, simultaneous-coverage, and conic-programming architecture; they do not give the joint attainable-bias min--max frontier or the order-sharp SOCP-to-frontier ratio proved here. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, equation (13) and Sections 3.2--3.4) provide scalar worst-case-bias plus standard-error logic over a convex Gaussian regression class. Anderson (1955, Theorem 1) supplies the weak moving-set inequality used by the separate strict zero-bias Loewner result. Kallus (2020) motivates the dual-norm bias--variance optimization analogy. Pataki (2013) and Jeyakumar, Kum, and Lee (2008) support the facial-reduction substrate for the degeneracy-safe conic certificate. Basu, Pollack, and Roy (2006, Theorems 13.11 and 14.16) support terminating real-closed-field quantifier elimination and sign-condition sampling with the stated sample-representation bounds; the note does not attribute a bit-complexity bound for the complete certificate construction to those excerpts. The present results retain the declared known-covariance experiment; they do not claim a covariance-estimation or published-class transfer theorem. \texttt{scpi} and \texttt{augsynth::multisynth} are named as potential software consumers of the geometry and optimization, not as covered procedures.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact full-class characterization is a finite-dimensional attained min--max functional, but evaluating correlated shifted Gaussian-cube probabilities and globally optimizing that generally nonconic objective can be computationally harder than solving the Bonferroni SOCP. The order-sharp family shows that the square-root spectral condition-number loss of fixed Bonferroni calibration cannot be removed uniformly, although particular covariance and donor geometries may yield a much smaller gap. The covariance remains known and prespecified; covariance estimation, selective donor choice, outcome-dependent weights, and transfer to a published estimator class are outside this version. The facial-reduction equivalence concerns strict \(\Gamma\) improvement on arbitrary degenerate faces and is not a general strict-\(W\) criterion. Its exact algebraic construction and verifier are proved to terminate, but no quantitative bit-complexity or practical-efficiency guarantee is asserted.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Finite-sample SOCP coverage, the exact full bounded-mean attainable-bias frontier, the covariance-domination sandwich, its square-root condition-number order-sharpness, weak nested-support dominance, and the rational strict witnesses are theorem-level results. The exact formula uses all existing \(L\) and \(\delta\) values and maximizes over the jointly attainable bias set; it does not assume simultaneous coordinatewise endpoint attainment. On the zero-bias class, \texttt{thm:correlated-gaussian-exact-frontier} additionally gives a strict Loewner covariance criterion, while \texttt{thm:disjoint-diagonal-exact-frontier} gives the explicit product root. The exact finite certificate in \texttt{thm:degenerate-iff-gap-certificate} characterizes strict SOCP improvement on degenerate faces and admits a terminating construction and verifier, but carries no quantitative runtime bound. Unknown covariance, covariance confidence sets, random donor selection, outcome-dependent weights, direct coverage claims for the Ben-Michael--Feller--Rothstein estimator, and coverage claims for \texttt{scpi} or \texttt{augsynth::multisynth} are outside the paper. Correlated Gaussian-max numerical calibration is a post-solve refinement.

statement_notes.justification: Strict improvement of the fixed-Bonferroni SOCP must remain decidable and independently checkable when primal or dual solutions lie on degenerate cone faces. The theorem gives an exact finite primal--facial-dual certificate and proves termination of its algebraic construction and verifier without asserting an unsupported complexity rate.
statement_notes.consumer: An implementer or auditor can use the certificate to verify \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\) from finite rational design inputs even under degeneracy. This certifies the SOCP surrogate comparison; it does not by itself certify strict improvement of the exact honest-width frontier \(W_s\), and it makes no runtime guarantee for \texttt{scpi} or \texttt{augsynth::multisynth}.
